hypotheses.reasoning: accounts-db's data volume filled up. A disk-usage warning at 95% (#477, WAL/binlog growth 595MB/h) was followed by 99% (#910, growth 816MB/h). Once the disk was full, inserts into the accounts table began failing: account-svc logged 'could not extend file ... No space left on device' (#1254, #1347, #1468), and accounts-db reported the same error at the storage layer (#1257, #1378, #1469). Those failed inserts surface at the edge as POST /login 500s from account-svc (edge-proxy #1289, #1470, #1883). Reads stay healthy because they don't need new space. The disk fill is the origin; the 500s are downstream.

billing-reconciler logs checksum constraint violations on invoice_archive rows in 2019 partitions starting around 13:34. They affect only the billing archive, not the login path, so this is a separate problem and not the cause of the login 500s.

verdict.recommendedAction: Immediately free disk space on the accounts-db data volume (find and prune the WAL/binlog growth source) or extend the volume so inserts can resume. Then confirm account-svc inserts succeed and POST /login 500s drop. Add a disk-usage alert with earlier thresholds. Separately, investigate the billing-reconciler invoice_archive checksum violations in the 2019 partitions as a distinct data-integrity issue.
